chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Studying with Mike Gunable; first trip to Atlantic City
summary: McRae studied with a strict teacher, Mike Gunable, then got an offer in Atlantic City where he met Claude Hopkins and heard Hilton Jefferson and Elmer Williams.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I played in the school band. Like I said before, when I -- I studied a lot. I studied off a fellow named Mike Gunable, a very

fine teacher. A very fine teacher. He was very fine. And I studied with him for quite a while. I forgotten how many years I studied with him.. It was during the time I was going to school. And we used to study on a Sunday and maybe twice a week. He was very strict. He gave you to do after you came in. things (inaudible) And he turned me out. (Inaudible) became a very outstanding tenor player, but I didn't play much around Philly when I was kid. I was young, in my 20's or something like that. I didn't play much around Philly. I had an offer to come to Atlantic City to play in one of the clubs there. And that's where I met Claude Hopkins. And he had a little small band there. And I heard Hilton Jefferson and Elmore Williams, the tenor player that wind up with Chick. But that was way before. There were those two guys, the finest tenor players that anybody wanted to listen to. They had (inaudible) a saxophone team --
